Two AWS pages disagree on when exam prices are refreshed (FAQ: 'updated annually in April'; before-testing: 'at least annually in May'). The book does not need the month; the miner records the disagreement and the writer states neither.

The exam guide's own wording for multiple response is 'two or more correct responses out of five or more response options' (d008). The familiar '(Select TWO.)' with exactly five options is a format observation from the sample questions, not an AWS rule; 'no partial credit' is a third-party claim (FREQUENCY section 4) and must not appear as a fact.

Items of kind 'heuristic' (reading order, qualifier meanings, the nine word groups) are role method text under SPEC.json grounding.heuristic: absolute words are allowed there, a number-with-unit needs a fact link. They are listed so that no section is missing, and they need no fact unless they state a number; the exam-English words themselves come from data/exam-english.json (orchestrator-owned, 9 groups, 0 words at planning time).

demand.question: How many questions does the SAA-C03 exam have in total, and how many are scored and unscored?
demand.hint: Exam page: '65 questions; either multiple choice or multiple response' (under 'Exam format'). Exam guide: 'The exam includes 50 questions that affect your score.' and 'The exam includes 15 unscored questions that do not affect your score.' Display value 65 with the split 50 + 15 as two supporting evidence items.

demand.question: How long is the exam (minutes)?
demand.hint: Exam page under 'Exam duration': '130 minutes'. The heading and the value are on separate lines; quote the row with its heading (show --around '130 minutes').
demand.registrar_note: Evidence is the AWS Training and Certification blog sentence (source tier 2): the exam page states 130 minutes only as a two-word value line that M4 cannot accept; the exam page stays the authority (fact note).

demand.question: How many unscored questions are there, can the candidate tell which they are, and why does AWS include them?
demand.hint: 'These unscored questions are not identified on the exam.' and 'every question is first administered in beta as an unscored question on an exam.' Teach: do not try to spot them; answer every question.

demand.question: Is there a penalty for guessing, and how is an unanswered question scored?
demand.hint: 'Unanswered questions are scored as incorrect; there is no penalty for guessing.' Behavior fact: needs two displays (B12).

demand.question: What is the passing score and on what scale is the result reported?
demand.hint: Exam guide: 'Your results for the exam are reported as a scaled score of 100–1,000. The minimum passing score is 720.' After-testing: 'The passing standard is represented by a scaled score of 700 for Foundational-level exams, 720 for Associate-level exams, and 750 for Professional-level and Specialty exams.' Display '720 on a scale of 100 to 1,000'.

demand.question: Does she need to pass each domain separately, or only the exam as a whole (compensatory scoring)?
demand.hint: 'The exam uses a compensatory scoring model, which means that you do not need to achieve a passing score in each section. You need to pass only the overall exam.' Matters for her: Secure 45% on the diagnostic does not fail her alone.

demand.question: Why is the score scaled rather than a raw count, and why does AWS say to use caution with section-level feedback?
demand.hint: After-testing: 'Scores for the AWS Certification exams are reported as scaled scores, rather than the raw number of questions scored correct.' and the modified Angoff and equating paragraphs. Exam guide: 'Use caution when you interpret section-level feedback.' FAQ #42: 'AWS does not publish exam passing scores' (contrast with the exam guide's 720: the guide wins; note the FAQ wording as a trap for the miner, not for the book).

demand.question: What are the two question types, exactly as the exam guide defines them (how many correct and incorrect responses each)?
demand.hint: 'Multiple choice: Has one correct response and three incorrect responses (distractors)' and 'Multiple response: Has two or more correct responses out of five or more response options'. Also 'There are two types of questions on the exam' (grounds the FREQUENCY claim that SAA-C03 has no ordering, matching or case-study items).

demand.question: What is a distractor, according to AWS, and why does that matter for how she eliminates options?
demand.hint: 'Distractors, or incorrect answers, are response options that a candidate with incomplete knowledge or skill might choose. Distractors are generally plausible responses that match the content area.' Teach: a plausible option is not a correct option; find the constraint it breaks.

demand.question: What are the four domains and their weights of scored content?
demand.hint: 'Content Domain 1: Design Secure Architectures (30% of scored content)', Domain 2 26%, Domain 3 24%, Domain 4 20%. One fact per domain (exam-domain-1-weight ... exam-domain-4-weight) or one fact with four values; the mock split 20/17/15/13 of 65 in RULINGS is derived from these.

demand.question: What does the exam validate and what is it based on (the Well-Architected Framework), and what are the six pillars?
demand.hint: 'The exam validates a candidate's ability to design solutions based on the AWS Well-Architected Framework.' Pillars page: 'the six pillars of operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, and sustainability'. Two facts (exam-validates-well-architected, wa-six-pillars).
demand.registrar_note: The six pillars are a well-architected namespace fact (home chapter 02); chapter 01 links it.

demand.question: What is the ESL accommodation: how many extra minutes, who can request it, when must it be requested, and does it carry over to later exams?
demand.hint: Before-testing: 'A 30-minute exam extension is available upon request to non-native English speakers when taking an exam in English. The accommodation, "ESL +30," only needs to be requested once, prior to registering for an exam. It will apply to all future exam registrations with all test delivery providers.' FAQ #53 (partner section): 'request an ESL accommodation for an additional 30-minutes to complete the exam.' Day 1 of the calendar says 'request ESL +30 before booking'; the five request steps on the page can become a Try task (max 1 for this template).

demand.question: Must every accommodation be requested before scheduling, and who grants it?
demand.hint: 'Accommodations must be requested prior to scheduling each exam.' FAQ #33: 'Special accommodations will be arranged with the test delivery provider, prior to registering for your exam.'

demand.question: How long must she wait to retake after a fail, is there a limit on attempts, and must she pay again?
demand.hint: 'If you fail an exam, you must wait 14 calendar days before you are eligible to retake the exam. There is no limit on exam attempts. However, you must pay the full registration fee for each exam attempt.' Same sentence on both pages. Three facts or one with three values: exam-retake-wait (14 calendar days), exam-retake-attempts (no limit), exam-retake-fee.

demand.question: After passing, how long before the same exam can be taken again, and what if a new exam version appears?
demand.hint: 'Once you have passed an exam, you will not be able to retake the same exam for two years. If the exam has been updated with a new exam guide and exam series code, you will be eligible to take the new exam version.'

demand.question: When are results available, where, and is the pass/fail shown on screen at the end?
demand.hint: After-testing: 'Final results will be posted to your AWS Certification Account within five business days after the close of the exam.' FAQ #7: 'Most AWS Certification exams do not display your pass/fail result at the end of the test.' Two facts: exam-results-timing (5 business days, Exam History) and exam-no-result-on-screen.

demand.question: Until when can she reschedule or cancel without a fee, how many times can one appointment be rescheduled, and what happens if she misses the appointment?
demand.hint: Before-testing: 'You can reschedule your exam up to 24 hours before your scheduled exam time. Each exam appointment can only be rescheduled twice.' and 'Canceling your exam less than 24 hours prior to your appointment, or failing to appear for your appointment, will result in the forfeiture of your exam fee.' FAQ #9: 'Missing the exam does not result in a "fail" status.' Facts: exam-reschedule-window (24 hours), exam-reschedule-limit (twice), exam-missed-appointment.

demand.question: What does the exam cost, and is there a discount after a first certification?
